prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro railway; CBTC supervises separation, movement authority (MA), regulation. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (live view of positions, routes, alarms; selects holding/skip-stop/turnback/run-through after passenger impact and recovery assessed; confirms after Lantern shows action, trains, recovery time; produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice after confirming limits, speed, start, removal condition; monitors delay, adjusts regulation; records incident time, train, location, impact, first safe instruction; requests executed only if interlocking and CBTC agree; no vital intervention); Revenue Train Operator (sees MA, speed, location confidence; acknowledgements to Atlas, stale rejected); Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple (records track clearance before restoring route setting after detection anomaly); Cyber Security Officer (Cryptographic Key Management Appliance keys; no safety-logic change). Elements: Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern (regulating options from timetable variance, dwell, headway, routes; sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas; displays commanded/locked route, points, occupancy). North District Zone Controller, alias Marble (approach to East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon); South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid (West Junction Interlocking); compute MA, send to Atlas; report conflicts/unavailable routes; handover after odometer confirmation and receiving-zone validation. Route in MA only when overlap/flank protected; interlockings keep final vital authority; points detected, locked, proved; lost correspondence shortens/withdraws MA. Falcon holds route locked until release criteria; sends Axle Counter Reset Request (inhibited while route locked/train approaching). West Junction sends Route Release Exception List (retained hazard) and route state indications distinguishing delay from fault. Axle counters independent; conflicts apply more restrictive state. Platform Screen Door Controller sends closed-and-locked indications (cannot override MA). Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel: validates token bundle; enforces MA; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log; modes initialization, protected manual, ATO, fallback, cutout; radio loss: last validated MA. Dual Channel Odometer: independent distance inputs; divergence degrades. Train Radio Modem via Wayside Radio Access Network, alias Saffron (sends Radio Handover Audit File; coverage/capacity alarms); radio loss may hold trains. Safety Data Communication Network: vital authenticated messages; sends Clock Drift Sample Report; persistent faults escalated before regulation. Maintenance Diagnostic Server, alias Quarry; Service Timetable Server, Passenger Information Gateway, Voice Dispatch Console:

New part:
S117: The Voice Dispatch Console is used when direct verbal instruction is required, and the instruction is repeated back by the Revenue Train Operator before the action is treated as accepted.
S118: The Revenue Train Operator reports train condition, cab indications, passenger issues, and any local hazard that cannot be confirmed from the control room display alone.
S119: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server provides non-vital trend data that helps the Signal Maintenance Engineer determine whether an incident has an equipment cause or an operational cause.
S120: The Signal Maintenance Engineer advises the Line Traffic Controller on equipment recovery options, but the Line Traffic Controller remains responsible for service regulation decisions during the event.
S121: The Service Timetable Server is updated only through an approved timetable change workflow, and the Line Traffic Controller verifies that the revised plan is visible before relying on it for regulation.
S122: The Passenger Information Gateway receives the operational service state needed to align platform messages and train destination information with the current regulating plan.
S123: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance uses the sample report to verify that certificate validity windows and controller clocks remain within the permitted tolerance before operational use.
S124: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance produces the Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack under an approved maintenance window and records the change reference for later security audit.
S125: The Cyber Security Officer reviews certificate change records, access events, and unusual authentication failures before authorising normal operational reliance on the renewed security configuration.
S126: Authority review is performed after major incidents, degraded operations, and timetable interventions to confirm that each commanded movement remained consistent with interlocking state, controller intent, and recorded train response.
S127: This section describes the operational interfaces between the Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System and station equipment that affects departures, passenger information, and dispatcher awareness.
S128: Platform equipment is treated as part of the movement-authority environment when its state can prevent a train from arriving, dwelling, or departing safely.
S129: Platform Screen Door Controller produces the Platform Door Status Snapshot at each monitored platform face for operational use by the CBTC system.
S130: The door interface reports closed, locked, bypassed, inhibited, and faulted conditions using coded states that are interpreted consistently across the line.
S131: A departure command is not considered available to the Revenue Train Operator until the relevant platform door state is compatible with the requested direction of travel.
S132: North District Zone Controller suppresses platform departure authority when the associated berth reports an unsafe door interface state.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.

Revenue Train Operator (sees MA, speed, location confidence; acknowledgements to Atlas, stale rejected; repeats back voice instructions before acceptance; reports train condition, cab indications, passenger issues, local hazards; departure unavailable until door state compatible with direction).
